item.title: Apache Flink internals - TaskManager
item.description:
A TaskManager is the worker that runs a Flink job. The JobManager only picks a free slot and sends the task. After that, the records, the state, and the event-time clock live on this process.

  • Slots. Capacity is a fixed number of slots. Chained operators share one slot and one thread, so a record between them is a local call.
  • Direct exchange. A record for another task goes straight from this worker to that worker. When the receiver is full, this worker slows the sender.
  • Local state and time. Keyed state stays on the machine that owns the key. The task stamps event time and advances watermarks as records arrive.

item.title: Apache Flink internals - JobManager
item.description:
A JobManager is the process that takes a Flink job and runs it. It finds workers that have room, and keeps the job going until it finishes. The data itself is processed on those workers.

The program arrives in one of two ways. An application cluster already has the user JAR on the JobManager. It runs main() itself and copies that JAR into the BlobServer, so the workers can load it. A session cluster receives a client request: the client uploads the JAR, then submits the job. Either way the JobManager splits the program into tasks and starts them.

item.title: Apache Flink internals - cluster topology and client job submission
item.description: Apache Flink is a distributed engine for continuous (and bounded) dataflow programs. A job is a graph of operators; the runtime places parallel tasks on TaskManagers, keeps operator state local to those tasks, and advances time with watermarks so windows and timers close at well-defined points.
